headline: A Northern Gannet's Spectacular Dive Wins Global Photography Prize
meta_description: UK photographer Henry Spiers wins Bird Photographer of the Year 2026 with a dramatic image of a gannet diving off Scotland's coast, captured from over 24,000 e…
summary_short: A stunning photograph of a northern gannet erupting through Scottish waters has won the prestigious Bird Photographer of the Year award, with conservation donations reac…
body:
The 2026 Bird Photographer of the Year has been claimed by Henry Spiers from the United Kingdom, whose winning image 'Sunball Rocket' captures a northern gannet bursting through the ocean's surface in Scottish waters. Competing against over 24,000 submissions from photographers worldwide, Spiers's photograph also took first place in the Birds in the Environment category, earning him the £3,000 grand prize. The image showcases these remarkable seabirds in a moment of hunting intensity—the gannets dive from heights up to 30 metres at speeds reaching 60 miles per hour, their piercing yellow eyes ringed with blue circles scanning for prey. Yet Spiers's accompanying description reveals the duality of their existence: in the nest, these same birds tenderly stroke each other's white necks and nurture their young with careful devotion.

The competition also celebrated emerging talent: 16-year-old Parham Pourahmad from the United States won Young Bird Photographer of the Year with 'Moonlit Night', a great horned owl framed against a full moon. Pourahmad spotted a nesting pair in a park near his home and set out at dusk to capture their portrait—only to shift his aim when the full moon rose on the horizon, positioning himself to frame one owl against the celestial backdrop.

Beyond the artistry, the competition reflects a deeper commitment to wildlife protection. Organisers have donated over £5,000 to Birds on the Brink, a partner charity funding grassroots bird conservation projects globally. The message is clear: celebrating these creatures through photography fuels the will to protect them. Entries for next year's competition are already open to amateur and professional photographers alike.
quick_facts: Henry Spiers won with a gannet photograph taken in Scotland
Competition received 24,000+ submissions from around the world
Grand prize of £3,000 awarded to overall winner
16-year-old Parham Pourahmad won Young Photographer category
£5,000 donated to bird conservation charity partner
